plan.notes: Official Greensboro College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Academic Catalog. The catalog publishes degree requirements with no official semester sequence for this program - collected as a single requirements block (requirements_only). This plan covers the major requirements only (Required Courses plus Required Related Courses as printed); Greensboro College requires a minimum of 124 total credit hours for the degree, the balance being general education, all-college/disciplinary requirements and free electives, which are not part of this major block. Where the catalog prints only a block subtotal for a choose-from group, the group is recorded as one choice slot at the printed subtotal with the options named in the choice note; no per-option credits were invented. Catalog pp.229-231. The human development and family science multidisciplinary major includes a core of eight required courses from the departments of Psychology, Sociology and Education, including a research methods course in the social sciences and a capstone experience involving an internship in Child and Family Studies, Psychology, or Sociology, as printed. The major is offered as an on-ground program and as an online program; the academic degree requirements for each are the same, and students must choose either the on-ground program or the online program and may not switch from one to the other, as printed.

courses.title: Elective Group 1 course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Elective Group 1 - choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: BKE 3710 Behavior Guidance in Early Childhood Settings; BKE 3720 Emerging Literacy Development; BKE 3730 & BKE 3731 Supporting Early Human Development & Field Component; ELE 3755 Arts & Literature for Children; SPE 2900 & SPE 2901 Diverse Populations & Field Component.

courses.title: Elective Group 2 course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Elective Group 2 - choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: LGA 3250 Family Law; SOC 2010 Migration & Society; SOC 2207 Cultural Anthropology; SOC 3000 Social Theory; SOC 3359 Family Violence; SOC 3360 Juvenile Delinquency; SOC 3509 Race, Class, & Gender; SOC 3600 Human Services.

courses.title: Elective Group 3 course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Elective Group 3 - choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: PSY 2250 Death & Dying; PSY 2510 Health Psychology; PSY 2609 Human Sexuality; PSY 3200 Educational Psychology; PSY 3260 Counseling Theories; PSY 3300 Sensation & Perception; PSY 3350 Physiological Psychology; PSY 3450 Drugs & Behavior; PSY 4100 Learning & Memory; PSY 4300 Social Psychology.

courses.title: Capstone course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: PSY 4900 Senior Seminar; SOC 4900 Capstone: The Sociologist as an Agent of Change.

courses.title: Sociology course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: SOC 3309 Families in Society; SOC 3600 Human Services.

courses.title: Elective courses (3000+)
courses.choice_note: Electives, 8 credits as printed (block subtotal): two additional elective courses from Group 1, Group 2, or Group 3; courses must be numbered 3000+, as printed. The catalog notes that students will take five total elective courses as listed above, as printed.

courses.title: Requirements for B.A. degree only (2000+ courses)
courses.choice_note: Requirements for B.A. degree only, 8 credits as printed: ART, DAN, ECM, HIS, MUS, or THE 2000+ courses (block subtotal; no individual courses are listed).
